program_overview.title: Coding for Kids: Scratch to Games, Apps and AI
program_overview.tagline: A child who can drag two blocks together can start. Ten months later they have built games, a mobile app, Minecraft machines, an AI model and their first lines of Python.
program_overview.description:
This is our flagship coding journey for children aged 6 to 12, and it is built on a simple truth: kids learn to code by making things they want to show someone. Every week ends with something a child can demonstrate at the dinner table, a game, an animation, an app, a world, and every concept hides inside a project rather than a lecture.

The journey starts in Scratch, where logic is learned by snapping blocks: animations first, then real games with scores, levels and difficulty. From there the worlds get bigger: arcade games in Microsoft MakeCode, inventions on a simulated micro:bit, real mobile apps built in MIT App Inventor and installed on the family phone, coding inside Minecraft Education, first Lua scripts in Roblox Studio, and kid-safe AI, where children train their own image and sound models with Machine Learning for Kids and Teachable Machine and use them inside their own games. The final months build the bridge every parent asks about: from blocks to real typed code, with first Python turtle programs and a first hand-written web page.

The pace is honest: two live classes a week plus two to three hours of guided practice fits the journey in ten months, and younger children or busy terms stretch it to twelve without penalty, the batch adapts. Learning is checked the honest way too: classwork in every session, homework after every class, monthly challenges that mix new questions with earlier topics, and a final exam, a project plus a friendly viva, that decides the certificate. Real knowledge, real work, real projects, depth over dopamine.
what_makes_this_different: Every week ends with something a child can show: a game, an app, a world, a model, not a worksheet
Batches are grouped by age, so a 7-year-old is never racing an 11-year-old through the same material
The tools are the real ones schools and clubs use worldwide: Scratch, MakeCode, App Inventor, Minecraft Education, Roblox Studio
AI is taught kid-safe and hands-on: children train their own models with Machine Learning for Kids and Teachable Machine, no open chatbots
The course ends with a real bridge to typed code: first Python and a first hand-written web page, so the next step is natural
Real assessment, gently done: weekly homework, monthly mixed-review challenges, and a final project-plus-viva exam that decides the certificate, with a free retest after revision if needed

learning_path.phase_3: Bigger worlds and AI (Months 7-8): coding in Minecraft Education, first Lua in Roblox Studio, and training their own AI models
learning_path.phase_4: The bridge to real code (Months 9-10): data projects, interactive stories, first Python, a first web page, and the final capstone

career_outcomes: A portfolio of 40+ real projects: finished games, a working mobile app, Minecraft builds, an AI model and first Python programs
Computational thinking that shows up at school: sequencing, logic, debugging and patience with hard problems
A confident, natural step into our Python for Kids, Roblox, Minecraft or Web Development courses
Screen time converted from consuming to creating, with safe digital habits taught alongside

faqs.question: What does my child build in this coding course?
faqs.answer: More than 40 real projects across ten months: animations and complete games in Scratch, arcade games in MakeCode, micro:bit inventions, a real mobile app built in MIT App Inventor and installed on a family phone, coding projects inside Minecraft Education, a Roblox world with first Lua scripts, AI models they train themselves, and finally their first typed Python programs and a hand-written web page. Every project is the child’s own work, reviewed by the teacher.

faqs.question: What age should my child be to start coding?
faqs.answer: The course runs from age 6 to 12, and batches are grouped by age: 6 to 8 year olds start gently and stay in visual tools longer, while 9 to 12 year olds move faster and reach Roblox scripting and Python sooner. Only comfortable reading is needed, no typing skill and no prior coding.

faqs.question: How long does it take a child to learn coding?
faqs.answer: The journey from zero to the final capstone takes most children 10 months at 2 live classes a week. The syllabus deliberately keeps 2 months of margin in hand: younger children or busy school terms stretch the same journey to 12 months with no rushing and no penalty. Real progress shows immediately, a child has a working animation in the very first class.

faqs.question: How is my child assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. There is classwork in every session, a small homework build after every class, and a monthly challenge that mixes new questions with earlier topics so skills stay sharp instead of fading. Each phase ends with a cumulative check, and the course ends with a final exam: a capstone demo plus a friendly viva and a mixed quiz. Passing earns the certificate; a child who falls short gets focused revision and a free retest. It is all gentle, and all real: we optimize for real knowledge, not a stream of feel-good badges.

faqs.question: Is this just more screen time?
faqs.answer: It is the opposite kind of screen time. Instead of consuming videos and games, children spend the hours making them: designing, building, testing and fixing their own projects. Parents consistently report the shift, the child starts asking how things work instead of just asking for the tablet. Safe digital habits are taught explicitly alongside.

faqs.question: How is AI taught to children this young?
faqs.answer: Hands-on and kid-safe. Children train their own image and sound models using Machine Learning for Kids and Google’s Teachable Machine, both built for classrooms, then use those models inside their own games, a pet that reacts to sounds, a game controlled by gestures. There are no open chatbots in the kids’ course; the point is understanding how AI learns, including how it gets things wrong.

faqs.question: Which platforms are used, and are they free?
faqs.answer: The core platforms, Scratch, Code.org, MakeCode, MIT App Inventor, Tinkercad and Teachable Machine, are free and browser-based. Minecraft Education and Roblox Studio are free to build in, with accounts set up together with a parent. A computer or laptop with internet is enough; no hardware kits are required, the micro:bit is taught in its full browser simulator.

faqs.question: What happens after this course?
faqs.answer: The final phase builds the bridge on purpose: children finish having already written first Python programs and a first web page. From there they step naturally into our Python for Kids, Roblox Game Coding, Minecraft Coding or Web Development for Kids courses, choosing the direction that pulled them hardest during the journey.

faqs.question: How much do classes cost each month?
faqs.answer: ₹1,499 per month for group classes, which include 2 live classes a week in batches of no more than 10 kids. Smaller mini batches of 3-4 students are ₹2,999 per month, and dedicated 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. For students outside India, prices are set per country and shown on this page in the local currency.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial class?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can book a free demo at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact with zero commitment, and many parents sit in on the demo to see the teaching style for themselves. We hold a 4.9 rating across 547 Google reviews, and the demo class is where most of those families started.

faqs.question: Are these live classes or videos?
faqs.answer: Every session is a live 1-hour online class taught by a real teacher; we never substitute pre-recorded videos. Groups stay small and interactive, so children build along during class rather than just watching, and the teacher sees and fixes small confusions before they grow.
